name: At home
kid: Little parcels of data zoom through the air, down a cable and along a glass thread to the internet – and the video comes back the same way!
nerd: At home, packets leave over 802.11 Wi-Fi, are bridged onto Ethernet at the access point, NATed by the home router and forwarded over a fibre uplink to the ISP.

describe.kid: A cut-away house sits on green hills. The path starts at your phone, hops by Wi‑Fi to the access point, runs by cable to the router, then follows fibre to the internet cloud. Parcels go out as requests and back as video.
describe.nerd: The home view shows the LAN path from phone to access point, router and fibre uplink. Packets go upstream over Wi‑Fi, Ethernet and GPON. Video packets return downstream along the same path.

router.kid: The router is the front door of your home. It writes your home’s address on the parcel and remembers who asked.
router.nerd: NAT rewrites the private source address 192.168.1.23 to the public 203.0.113.7 and tracks the connection so replies find their way back.

internet.nerd: Access network (PON/OLT), an aggregation layer (L2 backhaul to the BNG), the ISP’s MPLS core, then either settlement-free peering at an IXP or paid transit, ending at a CDN cache close to you. Each shaded area is one operator’s network.
